# Authenticated native administration

The three server tools require the existing `max_access: admin`, `auth_required: true`, and a nonempty bearer token. The HTTP transport validates that bearer. Defaults remain unchanged; no network binding or credentials are altered by this implementation. The tools belong to the existing `server` category.

- `server_tick_status {}` reads `world_name`, `session_id`, `minecraft_version`, `dimension`, `server_tick`, `world_game_time`, `tick_rate`, `milliseconds_per_tick`, `frozen`, `stepping`, `step_ticks_remaining`, `sprinting`, `runs_normally`, and `active_recorders`. Server ticks and persistent world game time are separate clocks. The rate is the configured target, not measured achieved TPS.
- `server_admin_command {expected_session, command, dimension?}` executes one single-line vanilla command, with an optional leading slash, up to 32,768 characters. The dimension defaults to the overworld. The command source is console with explicit OWNER permission (level 4), no player actor, captured feedback, and no admin-chat broadcast. Explicit command effects (for example `tellraw`, `tp`, `stop`, or `reload`) remain the command's responsibility and are not rolled back.
- `server_tick_control {expected_session, action, rate?, ticks?}` supports `rate` (finite 1..10000), `freeze`, `unfreeze`, `step`, `step_stop`, `sprint`, and `sprint_stop`. Step/sprint require 1..1,000,000 ticks; other actions reject irrelevant parameters. These use Minecraft's normal tick commands.

All mutations compare the expected session and require no active native recorder in the same server-thread task before dispatch. This prevents an arbitrary command/function from silently changing a recording's clock. Completed retained recordings do not block commands. Status may be read while recording. The client lifecycle helpers can bind the exact integrated server to `NativeTelemetry.sessionFor(server)`; closing telemetry clears that association.

Command responses include the actual post-command tick state, `before`, `command`, `permission_level: 4`, `success`, `callback_count`, summed vanilla `result`, `feedback`, `errors`, and `output_truncated`. Feedback is bounded to 128 messages/32,768 characters. Syntax errors are captured; failed vanilla callbacks are reported with feedback. No synchronous callback is explicitly unconfirmed, never success. A positive callback confirms immediate command execution only: reload, step, sprint and other delayed effects require subsequent status/readback. Connection loss or timeout does not prove that a command was unapplied; do not retry mutations blindly.

The old `command_execute` tool is unchanged. Offline tests verify validation, session/thread/recorder guards, explicit authenticated admission, result handling and feedback bounds. Compiling against Java 26.3 checks native APIs. Live command/tick behavior still requires root's controlled integration test.
